subject: SLA template — maintenance carveouts & monthly availability reconciliation
messages:
From: Eva Morales <eva@brightleafhealth.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@brightleafhealth.com
Date: 2026-10-11T09:07:00-07:00
Subject: SLA template: maintenance carveouts and monthly availability reconciliation

Hi Rachel,

Thanks again for the demo last week — Brightleaf is excited about Redwood's latency profile for inference workloads. Before we can move to a trial PO, procurement has a couple of asks around the standard SLA template you sent over: specifically how maintenance carveouts are defined and how monthly availability shortfalls reconcile into credits.

Key points from our side:
- We need clarity on planned maintenance windows (notification lead times, max weekly window).
- If an availability incident triggers credits, procurement wants a deterministic monthly reconciliation process (how credits are calculated and applied to the invoice).
- In the case of prolonged partial interruptions (degraded latency but not full outage), what remedy schedule applies?

I'm attaching our internal checklist — can you send a proposal that shows a practical carveout definition and a simple monthly credit schedule we can review? Also please flag any leadership approvals required for exceptions.

Best,
Eva Morales
Head of Procurement
Brightleaf Health
Attachment: Brightleaf_Redwood_SLA_Request_20261011.pdf

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Eva Morales <eva@brightleafhealth.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-11T11:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SLA template: maintenance carveouts and monthly availability reconciliation

Hi Eva — thanks for the clear checklist. Attaching a concise proposal that addresses each point (see Redwood_SLA_Template_v2.docx). High-level summary below; full details are in the attached doc and the reconciliation workbook.

Summary of proposed changes:
- Planned maintenance: 72 hours notice for any non-urgent maintenance; standard weekly maintenance carveout limited to a rolling 4-hour window per calendar week per region. Emergency maintenance (safety/patches) will be announced as soon as feasible and classified separately.
- Monthly reconciliation: credits computed pro-rata by minute of unavailable time below the monthly uptime baseline, with a monthly cap equal to 10% of that month’s Redwood invoice. We provide an itemized reconciliation report by the 5th business day following the month.
- Degraded latency: define latency SLOs (p50/p95/p99) in the template. Remedies for latency degradation are tiered: first threshold triggers monitoring alert and remediation SLA; repeated breaches escalate to pro-rata crediting (schedule in workbook).

Attachments: Redwood_SLA_Template_v2.docx, Monthly_Remedy_Schedule.xlsx

Next steps: if these match Brightleaf's needs, we can document the exceptions (if any) and route to legal and your procurement contacts. Monica / Karthik — can you review the monthly cap language and confirm we're comfortable with 10% cap + pro-rata calculation?

—Rachel
Rachel Kim
Director, Customer Success 
Redwood Inference
Attachment: Redwood_SLA_Template_v2.docx

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-12T10:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SLA template: maintenance carveouts and monthly availability reconciliation

Thanks Rachel — quick internal reply before we send to Brightleaf.

A few product/finance notes:
- 99.95% baseline uptime is reasonable for their workload given our regional redundancy; if they need 99.99% we should price a Dedicated pool or higher commitment.
- The 4-hour rolling weekly carveout is okay, but we should specify that maintenance scheduled in overlapping windows across regions will not multiply carveouts — carveout applies per-customer/per-region.
- Monthly cap: 10% is acceptable for standard hosted; if they want exceptions (larger cap or no cap) we tag as enterprise terms and escalate to sales/leadership.
- Latency remedies: confirm the p95 remediation threshold at 350ms for their expected token sizes; if they push lower we include a latency SLA uplift charge.

I also suggest adding an "operational grace" clause for the first 60 days of a new workload where we provide enhanced monitoring and waive the monthly cap for one claim to help them ramp. That might be a helpful commercial concession during procurement.

Karthik, assigning to you to confirm the legal wording for the pro-rata formula and that the monthly reconciliation timeline (report by 5th business day) is workable for finance.

—Monica
Monica Patel
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Eva Morales <eva@brightleafhealth.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Brightleaf Health Procurement <procurement@brightleafhealth.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-13T15:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SLA template: maintenance carveouts and monthly availability reconciliation

Rachel / team — this looks very constructive. A few quick items from procurement:
- The 72-hour notice and 4-hour weekly carveout are acceptable, please add explicit language on notification channels (email + portal notice) and an escalation contact for scheduled maintenance.
- We like the monthly reconciliation approach; procurement will need the reconciliation report with a one-line summary table we can include in our invoice matching process.
- Regarding the 10% monthly cap: Brightleaf prefers to have an exception where prolonged incidents over two consecutive months can be escalated to a one-time credit above the cap pending executive review. Would Redwood be open to that as a controlled exception?

For next steps: please route the revised template to Laura Bennett at Redwood for leadership acknowledgment and then share a DocuSign-ready version for our procurement team. Once legal signs off on the pro-rata formula (Karthik), we can issue the trial PO and target a mid-November start.

Thanks — looping in procurement@brightleafhealth.com for visibility.

Best,
Eva Morales
Head of Procurement
Brightleaf Health
